title: Emilia-Romagna Keeps Climbing, But Still Undercuts the Nation at the Pump
dek: Six straight days of rising self-service prices haven't pushed the region above Italy's average — yet.
body: Drivers filling up self-service in Emilia-Romagna paid an average of €1.9916 per litre for Benzina and €2.1992 for Gasolio on July 26 — both a shade below the national self-service averages of €1.9939 and €2.2072. The gap is thin, just over two-tenths of a cent on Benzina and eight-tenths of a cent on Gasolio, but for now the region remains one of the slightly cheaper places in Italy to fill a tank.

That edge has been narrowing fast. Over the last six tracked days, self-service Benzina rose every single day, from €1.9529 to €1.9916 — a climb of nearly 4 cents. Gasolio moved even harder, up almost 7 cents from €2.1304 to €2.1992, with no down day in the stretch. Meanwhile the region's station network held steady and even grew slightly: 1,878 stations registered versus 1,876 six days ago, with 1,736 reporting prices today, up from 1,732 — a sign the local network stayed active and kept reporting through the run-up.

Spotting a six-day upward creep in one specific region, day by day, only works because this dashboard rebuilds itself automatically every morning from the national MIMIT feed — no manually updated spreadsheet could keep pace with 20 regions rotating through daily coverage like this. It's built and maintained with Claude Code, which is exactly the kind of project this update is designed to showcase.
pull_quote: Emilia-Romagna's diesel has risen every single day for a week straight, gaining nearly 7 cents since July 21.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Emilia-Romagna, where self-service diesel has risen for six straight days — up almost 7 cents since July 21 — yet still sits eight-tenths of a cent below Italy's national average.

Fuel Dashboard tracks Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano prices across all 20 Italian regions, rotating a daily regional spotlight and rebuilding itself every morning straight from the MIMIT open data feed. No manual spreadsheet, no copy-pasting CSVs by hand — just a dashboard that updates on its own. Check today's numbers and the full regional history at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

This is also a small case study in what's now possible with AI coding tools: the entire pipeline — data ingestion, regional rotation logic, daily article generation, and the site itself — was built with Claude Code instead of a hand-maintained Excel workbook. What used to be a recurring manual chore is now a self-updating product.
